title: I spent a day at a robot “carnival” in Shanghai. Here’s what I saw.
gist: China made nearly 90% of the more than 13,000 humanoid robots delivered worldwide last year, and embodied AI is written into its latest five-year plan; a Shanghai R&D-park carnival shows the domestic playbook is as much public acclimatization — robot dog toys, martial-arts demos, half-marathons — as engineering, even while safety, cost and battery life still cap real-world utility.

insights.claim: Nearly 90% of the more than 13,000 two-armed, two-legged robots delivered globally last year were made in China, meaning the humanoid supply chain is already concentrated in a single country before the category has a proven mass-market application.
insights.speaker: You Xiaoying
insights.so_what: Anyone building humanoid applications outside China faces a supply chain and cost structure set by Chinese OEMs — the same dynamic that played out in drones and solar.
insights.quote: Nearly 90% of the more than 13,000 two-armed, two-legged robots delivered globally last year were made in China.
insights.locator: Humanoid robots are having a moment in China

insights.claim: Embodied AI — embedding artificial intelligence into physical systems — was a key facet of China's latest five-year plan, giving humanoid development state-backed policy support rather than purely venture funding.
insights.speaker: You Xiaoying
insights.so_what: State-plan inclusion implies subsidized capacity and price pressure — model humanoid unit economics assuming below-cost Chinese competition.
insights.quote: Embedding the technology into physical systems—an idea called embodied AI—was a key facet of China’s latest five-year plan, and companies here are already world leaders in humanoids.
insights.locator: The popular machines are part of the country’s strategy

insights.claim: The Shanghai R&D hub hosting the carnival houses more than 100 companies researching, developing, manufacturing and marketing robotic technology, indicating cluster density rather than a handful of national champions.
insights.speaker: You Xiaoying
insights.so_what: Dense supplier clusters compress iteration cycles and component costs — a structural advantage Western humanoid startups cannot easily replicate.
insights.quote: This busy hub houses more than 100 companies that research, develop, manufacture, and market robotic technologies and equipment.
insights.locator: This busy hub houses more than 100 companies

insights.claim: Chinese robotics firms are running a coordinated consumer-exposure campaign — mall and tourist-attraction performances across several cities, bipedal robots running half-marathons in Beijing, carnival demos — treating public familiarity as a prerequisite to adoption.
insights.speaker: You Xiaoying
insights.so_what: Social license is being built ahead of product-market fit; watch consumer sentiment surveys as a leading indicator of Chinese humanoid deployment in service roles.
insights.quote: As this carnival takes place in Shanghai, shopping malls and tourist attractions in several other Chinese cities host humanoids that perform for crowds. In Beijing, bipedal robots are running half-marathons.
insights.locator: But Chinese firms are pushing forward

insights.claim: The author's on-the-ground read is that the PR campaign is working on public sentiment, with crowds chanting for more after martial-arts and acrobatic humanoid performances — though she explicitly limits the claim to that weekend in Shanghai.
insights.speaker: You Xiaoying
insights.so_what: Enthusiasm is measured at entertainment demos, not at price points — treat it as sentiment data, not demand data.
insights.quote: The PR campaign seems to be winning over hearts and minds—at least on this particular weekend in Shanghai.
insights.locator: The PR campaign seems to be winning over hearts and minds

insights.claim: Consumer robotics revenue at the event came from a low-priced adjacent product — a mini robotic dog toy parents were queuing to buy — rather than from the humanoids on stage.
insights.speaker: You Xiaoying
insights.so_what: The monetizable near-term category may be cheap quadruped toys and specialized bots, not bipedal humanoids — check where robotics firms actually book revenue.
insights.quote: Meters away from where parents and children are queued up to buy the robotic dog, two staffers teach youngsters how to make a quadrupedal robot walk up a flight of stairs.
insights.locator: Today, however, things are mostly for show

themes.theme: Unsolved constraints on the humanoid form

insights.claim: Humanoid progress has been slow outside China because of safety problems stemming from the machines' heft and need to balance on two legs, compounded by high prices and short battery life.
insights.speaker: You Xiaoying
insights.so_what: Battery energy density and safety certification are the gating variables; component-level progress there matters more than new humanoid model launches.
insights.quote: elsewhere humanoids’ progress has been slow, marred by safety challenges due to their heft and need to balance on two legs. High prices and short battery life have also limited their appeal.
insights.locator: Exposure matters, because elsewhere humanoids’ progress

insights.claim: Plenty of roboticists remain skeptical that the human form is the optimal shape for a robot at all, a dissent that sits directly against the capital flowing into bipedal humanoids.
insights.speaker: You Xiaoying
insights.so_what: Form-factor risk is real: capital concentrated in bipeds could be stranded if wheeled or task-specific designs win on cost and reliability.
insights.quote: Plenty of roboticists are skeptical that a human form is the best shape for a robot to take.

insights.claim: The commercial pitch from DexForce product manager Yang Duan is labor substitution — machines that free people from physical work and mundane chores — while the demonstrated tasks at the carnival were making coffee and folding T-shirts.
insights.speaker: You Xiaoying
insights.so_what: The gap between the labor-replacement narrative and the demonstrated task set (coffee, laundry folding) is the honest measure of how far commercialization is.
insights.quote: can free people from physical work and mundane chores,
insights.locator: Some of China’s most prominent robotics companies are building humanoids

insights.claim: The genuinely deployed robots at the hub are non-humanoid and task-specific — machines that transport heavy loads or inspect sewage pipes — while the humanoids were there mostly for show.
insights.speaker: You Xiaoying
insights.so_what: Revenue today sits in unglamorous specialized robotics; that is where to look for near-term cash flows rather than in humanoid headlines.
insights.quote: Many build specialized bots of all shapes that can do practical tasks, such as transporting heavy loads or inspecting sewage pipes.
insights.locator: Many build specialized bots of all shapes
